body.cap: Official Poster of 2025 SXSW Film & TV Festival | Image by SXSW

body.x: South by Southwest (SXSW) Conference and Festivals has revealed the lineup for its 32nd edition of the SXSW Film & TV Festival, which will occur from March 7 to 14, 2025. This year’s festival will open with the highly anticipated Apple TV+ series The Studio, created by Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg, who also serve as executive producers. The series stars Rogen as Matt Remick, a newly appointed studio head who navigates the turbulent world of Hollywood filmmaking.

The 2025 SXSW Film & TV Festival will showcase 96 feature films, including 82 world premieres. Highlights include Holland by Mimi Cave, Ash by Flying Lotus, Death of a Unicorn by Alex Scharfman, The Accountant 2 starring Ben Affleck, The Astronaut by Jess Varley, Drop by Christopher Landon, and The Makings of Curtis Mayfield directed by H.E.R. The festival will also feature 57 short films, 18 music videos, and an extensive lineup of episodic programming, including 16 TV projects with five world premiere series.

Claudette Godfrey, VP of Film & TV at SXSW, emphasized the festival’s commitment to bold storytelling: “The same undeniable creative electricity in The Studio runs through our 2025 program. This year’s lineup celebrates fearless storytellers who push boundaries and spark conversations in unexpected ways.”

The festival features a Headliner, Narrative Feature Competition, Documentary Feature Competition, Narrative Spotlight, midnighters, Global, 24 Beats Per Second, and Special Events. The TV program includes the Independent TV Pilot Competition, TV Spotlight, and TV Premiere sections. The XR Experience Program will highlight groundbreaking work in immersive storytelling, with 31 projects featured.

The Headliner section will showcase high-profile premieres, including The Accountant 2, Ash, Death of a Unicorn, Drop, and Holland. Meanwhile, the Narrative and Documentary Feature competitions will spotlight emerging voices and powerful storytelling.

body.cap: A Still Image from Fly To You, Directed by Youngyun Song and Sngmoo Lee | Image Credit: Youngsam Jung

body.x: The XR Experience Program will present 31 projects, including 15 in the XR Experience Competition and 16 in the XR Experience Spotlight. Immersive projects such as the 1906 Atlanta Race Massacre and The Secret Life of Monsters—The Gateway Experience will redefine storytelling through interactive and virtual reality elements. Among projects featured in this category, Fly to You, directed by Youngyun Song and Sngmoo Lee of Korea National University of Arts, will have a North American Premiere. The only work from South Korea to be part of the competing lineup of 2025 SXSW, Fly To You presents the tragic story of 85-year-old Kang Songjeol, who struggles with her childhood memory of abrupt separation from her cousin during the Korean War.

body.cap: Youngyun Song (left) and Sngmoo Lee (right) | Image Credit: Youngyun Song and Kyunghee Kim

body.x: The competition winners, including the Narrative Feature, Documentary Feature, Short Film, and XR Experience Awards, will be announced on March 12. The Audience Awards, certified by Maxwell Locke & Ritter, will follow. SXSW remains an Academy Award-qualifying festival, with its Best Animated, Best Narrative, and Best Documentary Short Film winners eligible for Oscar nominations.

In 1987, SXSW became a premier global platform for creative professionals in film, television, music, tech, and culture. The festival continues to expand, with SXSW Sydney launching in 2023 and SXSW London debuting in 2025. SXSW 2025 is driven by Rivian and sponsored by Epidemic Sound, Redbreast, and The Austin Chronicle.
